headline: Merge sorted rows of the pair-sum matrix
statement: Given sorted nums1 and nums2, return k value pairs using one entry from each array with the smallest sums. Equal values from different positions supply distinct pairs; ties may be returned in any order.
constraints: Both arrays are nonempty and sorted nondecreasingly.
intuition: For one value from the first sorted array, pairing it with the second array gives a sorted row of sums. Treat these rows as sorted lists. Keep each row's next pair in a heap, take the smallest pair, then advance only that row.
approach: Seed up to k rows with their pair at column zero.
Pop the heap's smallest sum and append its two values.
Push the next column from that same row if one exists.
Repeat until k pairs have been returned.
correctness: The heap holds the smallest unreturned pair in every seeded row, so its minimum is the next globally smallest pair among those rows. Unseeded rows begin no earlier than the kth row; the k seeded row starts already provide k sums no greater than any unseeded start. Thus omitting those rows cannot invalidate the first k sums.
bruteForce: Build every pair and sort by sum, requiring O(mn log(mn)) time and O(mn) space.

complexity.space: O(min(m, k)) auxiliary plus O(k) output
complexity.explanation: Heap size is at most the number of seeded rows; each emitted pair causes at most one insertion.

pitfalls: Keep array indices to preserve duplicate-pair occurrence count.
Push only the next column of the popped row.
Different tied pairs can all be correct.
